cohort: Pregnant women in the Sidama region of southern Ethiopia, enrolled between 20 and 37 weeks of gestation, including those with preeclampsia and a normotensive comparison group, followed until 12 weeks postpartum.
finding: Postpartum women with preeclampsia experienced significantly lower overall health-related quality of life (HRQoL) compared to normotensive women, though HRQoL improved over time from 6 to 12 weeks postpartum, with early neonatal death and preterm birth negatively impacting HRQoL.
